question: Should OpenClaw add an opt-in sandbox-to-ACP bridge now, fold this into the broader execution-backend design, or keep ACP blocked from sandboxed sessions?
rationale: The request crosses a sandbox-to-host process execution boundary and would define a public security/config contract, so automation should not choose the permanent trust model.

options.title: Design Narrow Bridge
options.body: Define an explicit opt-in host bridge with requester allowlisting, spawn/steer/cancel verbs, audit logs, rate limits, docs, and live Docker/acpx proof.

options.title: Fold Into Execution Backends
options.body: Use the broader backend/profile work as the design home and keep this issue as the sandboxed ACP acceptance case.

options.title: Keep Blocked
options.body: Preserve the current fail-closed behavior and document that ACP must run from non-sandboxed sessions or inside the containerized harness setup.

recommendation.title: Design Narrow Bridge
recommendation.body: Define an explicit opt-in host bridge with requester allowlisting, spawn/steer/cancel verbs, audit logs, rate limits, docs, and live Docker/acpx proof.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the clearest combined signal from the direct slash-command guard, documentation, and current security/product boundary context.
